items.subject: Grocery: 7 NEW price flag(s) - 2026-08-02
evidence: PACKBASIS furniture-polish IS A REAL WRONG CROWN (the one code-actionable flag): Sam's Club | 'Pledge Furniture Enhancing Polish Spray, Lemon, 3ct., 29 oz.' | $12.52 | published size '3 ct 29 oz', basis 'size 87 oz', per-unit 0.1439/oz, CROWN. Sam's OWN unit price on the raw row is $4.17/ea = 12.52/3, i.e. the pack holds 3 EACHES, and 29 oz is the pack TOTAL: 29/3 = 9.67 oz per can, matching the 9.7 oz single Pledge/Kroger/Favor cans at FF, Hy-Vee, Baker's and Walmart to within 0.4 percent. True per-unit = 12.52/29 = 0.4317/oz, which makes the real crown Fareway 'Behold Furniture Polish, Lemon' $2.99 / 12.5 oz = 0.2392/oz. The same bug also understates the non-crown all-purpose-cleaner row 'Pledge Multisurface Cleaner, Rainshower, 3 ct., 29 oz.' (same $12.52, same $4.17/ea, published 0.1439/floz vs true 0.4317).

MECHANISM MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: across 2,526 unique Sam's names (sams-deals-2026-07-29 + 2026-08-01, sams-regular-2026-08-01 + 07-14), 42 names carry a count-plus-weight idiom; 7 are live board rows. 5 of those 7 are CORRECT because Sam's weight-based unitPrice validated the quantity at capture (Febreze 32.4 oz total, Clorox 363 fl oz total, Drano 160, Clorox TBC 144, Shearer's 96 = 2 x 48). The 2 wrong rows are exactly the rows where Sam's unitPrice is per-EACH, which validates only the count, so build-sams-deals' Get-NamePack paired the adjacent '29 oz.' as a PER-ITEM size (emitting '3 ct 29 oz') and compare-deals' count-first multipack branch multiplied 3 x 29 = 87 oz. The idiom is genuinely ambiguous at capture: 'Clorox Ultra Clean Tablets Toilet Bowl Cleaner, 6 ct., 3.5 oz.' is per-item (3.5 oz per tablet, Sam's $2.30/ea x 6 = $13.78 checks), while Pledge '3 ct., 29 oz.' is a total. Same grammar, opposite meanings, undecidable without peers.

PACKBASIS hummus (already-open flag, kept as the clean twin): 'Member's Mark Classic Hummus Singles 2.5 oz., 16 ct.' $5.58 published 0.1395/oz is CORRECT (16 x 2.5 = 40 oz; weight-first idiom is per-item); the auditor's as_pack_total reading 2.232/oz is the false one. Any fix must leave this row alone.

SANITY Coriander (ground) SETTLED AS REAL: Fareway raw row 'Badia Spices Coriander, Ground' $1.68 marked down from regular $2.49, size 1.75 oz, as_of 2026-07-31, link slug .../257999-badia-spices-coriander-ground-1-75-oz confirms the size. 1.68/1.75 = 0.96/oz. Runner-up Baker's 'Tampico Coriander Ground' $1.69 / 1 oz = 1.69/oz. The 43 percent gap is a markdown on a larger value-brand bottle, not a parse. This morning's earlier verification and this one now agree from the raw capture.

surface_fix.what: Take the two wrong-basis Sam's Pledge rows off the board via the known-wrong intake, then republish. furniture-polish crown becomes Fareway Behold 0.2392/oz (verified real everyday row); all-purpose-cleaner keeps its crown (Walmart) and simply loses the understated Sam's row.
surface_fix.exact_change: add-known-wrong rulings for: furniture-polish | Sam's Club | 'Pledge Furniture Enhancing Polish Spray, Lemon, 3ct., 29 oz.' (and the '3 ct.,' spaced variant) and all-purpose-cleaner | Sam's Club | 'Pledge Multisurface Cleaner, Rainshower, 3 ct., 29 oz.', reason: real price, wrong basis - '29 oz' is the pack total (3 x 9.67 oz) but the engine multiplies the name's count into it, publishing 0.1439 instead of 0.4317 per oz. Rows stay blocked until a size-verified recapture exists.

items.root_cause: Sam's writes two opposite meanings into one grammar: in 'X oz., N ct.' (weight-first) the weight is per-item, in 'N ct., X oz.' (count-first) the weight is usually the pack total, and sometimes (Clorox tablets) per-item. When Sam's unitPrice is weight-based, build-sams-deals lets Sam's own arithmetic decide the quantity and the rows come out right (5 of the 7 live idiom rows). When Sam's unitPrice is per-each it validates only the COUNT, Get-NamePack's count-first pattern (build-sams-deals.ps1 ~line 164) then pairs the adjacent weight as per-item with no validation, and compare-deals' count-first multipack branch (compare-deals.ps1 line 182) multiplies. No capture-side or engine-side rewrite can decide the bare count-first idiom locally: even emitting a count-only size fails, because Get-UnitPrice falls back to parsing the NAME and multiplies again. The only decidable signal is PEERS: when stated-total divided by count reproduces the single-unit size other stores sell (29/3 = 9.67 vs 9.7), the multiplied basis is provably wrong. audit-pack-basis already computes both readings and caught this row; it is advisory, so the wrong crown published anyway.

root_fix.what: Promote the decidable subset of audit-pack-basis to a blocking check: when a board row's basis came from a count-times-size multiplication AND stated-size divided by count matches a peer store's single-unit size for the same commodity within 5 percent, that is the arithmetic fingerprint of a pack TOTAL and the row must hard-fail publish. The undecidable rest stays advisory exactly as today.
root_fix.exact_change: audit-pack-basis.ps1: for each finding, compute each_derived = stated_total / count; if any OTHER store's row on the same commodity has a parsed single-unit size within 5 percent of each_derived, mark the finding CONFIRMED and exit 2. guards.ps1: add the audit as a blocking gate. test-auditors.ps1: frozen must-fire fixture from the real Pledge row (count 3, stated 29 oz, peers 9.7 oz) that must exit 2 and name the commodity; frozen clean twin from the real hummus row (count 16, stated 2.5 oz per-item) that must stay exit 0. Fixtures frozen from these rows, never regenerated from the live board.

blast_radius.measured_by: No commodity include/exclude or corpus name changes ship in this item, so before/after routing is identical by construction for all 22,341 unique names in plan-2026-08-02-2.routing.json's corpus (its changes array contains zero entries caused by this item). The basis-side blast was measured separately: 42 count-plus-weight Sam's names scanned, 7 live board rows checked one by one; exactly 2 rows (both Pledge, both $12.52 with $4.17-ea unit price) are wrong, 5 are validated correct by Sam's weight unitPrice, and the hummus row is confirmed correct. Post-fix: furniture-polish crown flips Sam's 0.1439 to Fareway 0.2392/oz; all-purpose-cleaner loses one non-crown row (7 stores to 6); no other cell's per-unit moves.

Both wrong-basis Pledge rows blocked via known-wrong (one spelling each; the spaced furniture-polish spelling is a DIFFERENT, correctly-priced row at 0.4317 and was deliberately left alone), crown corrected to Fareway Behold 0.2392/oz, and audit-pack-basis' peer-size fingerprint promoted to a blocking gate with frozen Pledge must-fire + hummus clean twin. items.premise_verified: TRUE, and re-proved from the raw rows rather than from the report. out/pack-basis-audit.json (09:03) carries furniture-polish published 0.1439 / as_pack_total 0.4317 / peer_cheapest 0.2392 / count 3 / size '3 ct 29 oz' / ad $12.52, matching the plan digit for digit. sams-deals-2026-08-01.json and sams-deals-2026-07-29.json both carry sams_unit_price '$4.17/ea' on the two Pledge rows, so 12.52/3 = 4.1733 proves three EACHES and the 29 oz is the pack total: 29/3 = 9.667 against 9.7 oz single cans at Family Fare, Hy-Vee and Baker's and 9.689 at Walmart, a 0.34 percent gap. The live board did publish Sam's at 0.1439/oz as the crown (verified on the live page at 375px before the fix: 'Sam's Club 14 cents/oz ... Pledge Furniture Enhancing Polish Spray'). Fareway 'Behold Furniture Polish, Lemon' $2.99 / 12.5 oz = 0.2392/oz is a real everyday row in the same cell. The hummus clean twin is confirmed too: 2.5/16 = 0.156 oz is a size no peer sells (8, 10 and 17 oz tubs), so the fingerprint cannot fire on it.
items.deviation:
THREE deviations, all measured.
(1) ONLY ONE of the two Pledge name spellings may be blocked, not both as exact_change says. Measured: the spaced spelling 'Lemon, 3 ct., 29 oz.' is the sams-regular row, whose size field is '29 oz' with NO count, and the engine prices it CORRECTLY at 12.52/29 = 0.4317/oz. Blocking it would have deleted a correct Sam's price. Only the '3ct.,' spelling (size '3 ct 29 oz', published 0.1439) is ruled. Post-rebuild the cell reads exactly right: crown Fareway Behold 0.2392/oz, and Sam's is still present at its own true 0.4317/oz.
(2) For all-purpose-cleaner the reverse holds: the '3ct.,' spelling the plan also asked for does not exist in ANY Sam's source file. The only row is 'Pledge Multisurface Cleaner, Rainshower, 3 ct., 29 oz.', which IS the wrong-basis one and is ruled. Sam's fell through to its own next-best real row, 'Fabuloso 2X Concentrated Multi-Purpose Cleaner, Lavender 210 fl. oz.' at 0.0523/floz, and Walmart keeps the crown at 0.0488 as predicted.
(3) Self-inflicted and repaired: the first ruling pass splatted -Name as a flat array, so PowerShell bound only the first value to -Name and the second fell through positionally to -ProductId. Seven entries carried a product NAME in product_id and audit-known-wrong was counting them as store-id-derived. All seven were cleared, and the four second names that genuinely needed their own ruling were re-added properly. The pork-tenderloin mojibake twin did NOT need one: measured, known-wrong-lib's normalizer maps both spellings to the same normal form.
The root_fix shipped as written. audit-pack-basis now exits 2 on the peer-size fingerprint, guards.ps1 delegates to it and printed 'ok no cell is cheapest because a pack TOTAL was multiplied by its own count', and test-auditors carries the real Pledge row as the frozen must-fire plus a new frozen hummus board as the clean twin.

evidence: MOVED=0 DROPPED=0 drift=0; the 4 new-contested names were routed with a first-match-wins simulation against commodities.json (503 rules): 'Deli Kitchen Jalapeno Pepper Hot Salsa' -> salsa (idx 78) SOUND, it is a salsa. 'Primal Kitchen Cilantro Lime Salad Dressing & Marinade' -> limes (idx 41) WRONG, a bottled dressing routes to fresh limes (cilantro idx 120 would claim it next). 'Private Selection Peach Halves with Almonds' -> peaches (idx 24) WRONG, it is a canned/jarred product (Baker's raw row: $9.99, 33 oz) on the FRESH peaches per-lb commodity; canned-peaches sits later at idx 186. None of the three wrong routings is a live board row today (checked by exact name against every store row of comparison-2026-08-02 and recipe-board-everyday) - they lose on price - but the mechanism is exactly the accidental-relevance-filter trap: the routing is wrong and only price keeps it off the board. The routing measurement also surfaced the same classes estate-wide: 11 protein-bar names claimed by cookies (Barebells, Atkins, Built Puff, Elevation, KiZE), 7 avocado-ranch dressings claimed by avocados, 7 canned-peach names claimed by fresh peaches (including Aldi 'Sweet Harvest Peaches IN 100 Juice 15 OZ'), plus 'Hidden Valley Cilantro Lime Ranch' and 'Stubb's Chiles, Lime & Ginger Pork Marinade' claimed by limes.

surface_fix.what: Release the wrong claims with class excludes, admit the released names to their true owners, then accept the soundness baseline.
surface_fix.exact_change: limes.exclude += '\bdressing\b','\bmarinade\b'; cilantro.exclude += '\bdressing\b','\bmarinade\b'; avocados.exclude += '\bdressing\b'; peaches.exclude += '\bhalves\b','\bjuice\b'; canned-peaches.include += 'peach\s+halves'; cookies.exclude += '\bprotein\s+bars?\b','\bparchment\b'; fresh-ginger.exclude += '\bmarinade\b' (second-order: without it, Stubb's marinade re-lands on fresh-ginger instead of bottled-marinade). After rebuild: audit-match-soundness.ps1, review, then -Accept.

items.root_cause: Single-word produce and snack includes (limes, peaches, cookies, avocados, cilantro) claim any product whose NAME mentions the word, and first-match-wins array order puts those commodities before the products' true owners (canned-peaches 186, protein-bars 223, ranch-dressing, bottled-marinade). Every contested name is the same shape: a processed product carrying a fresh-commodity word. The exclude vocabulary for the processed classes (dressing, marinade, halves, protein bar) simply did not exist on the fresh commodities.
items.root_fix_note: surface_fix IS the root fix for this class: the class tokens (dressing, marinade, protein bar, halves, juice) are category words, not brand words, so a store rename cannot disarm them the way brand-word excludes were disarmed on 2026-07-31.

items.subject: Grocery: 36 store(s) dropped from a commodity they carry - 2026-08-02
evidence: THE ALERT'S BLANKET PREMISE ('usually a too-strict include') IS FALSE FOR MOST OF THE 36: every candidate in coverage-gaps.json was routed against the live rules; the top candidate MATCHES and routes to the target commodity for 29 of 36 gaps. Those stores are absent for engine reasons the audit never checks, in three measured classes.

CLASS A - EACH-BASIS INEXPRESSIBLE (the largest): the commodity is priced per EACH but the store's current rows carry only weights or bags, so Get-UnitPrice returns null and the row drops. Walmart lemons/limes: only 'Fresh Lemons, 2 lb Bag' / 'Fresh Limes, 2 lb Bag' remain after the 2026-07-12 each-form rows aged out (same condition as the wow movers in 2026-08-02-04c64a). french-bread @ FF/Walmart: 'Fresh & Finest French Bread' 15 oz, 'Freshness Guaranteed French Bakery Bread Loaf, 14 oz, 1 Loaf' (the '14 oz' token wins the parse before '1 Loaf'). brownie-mix [each] @ FF: every FF row is a 16-18.4 oz box with no count. kale @ FF: bare 'Kale' priced per lb. watermelon @ Fareway: 'Half Seedless Watermelon' (and admitting a HALF as an each would be a wrong-basis crown, so its absence is CORRECT; a protective watermelon exclude '\bhalf\b' ships in this plan).

CLASS B - BAND-DROPPED VERIFIED-REAL PRICES: frozen-waffles @ Sam's 'Eggo Homestyle Waffles, Frozen Breakfast, 72 ct.' $9.87 = 0.1371/each, Sam's own unit price $0.14/ea, vs inline band_min 0.15. hand-sanitizer @ Sam's 'Member's Mark Hand Sanitizer, 67.6 fl. oz.' $5.93 = 0.0877/floz, Sam's own $0.09/foz, vs band_min 0.10. feta @ FF 'Athenos Feta Traditional Cheese Crumbles 4 Oz' $4.99 = 1.2475/oz vs band_max 1.20. All three are real shelf prices (two carry the store's own agreeing unit price) rejected by the magnitude net, so the audit re-reports them as gaps every day.

CLASS C - WRONG CLAIMS (the only genuine rule bugs in the item): berbere-seasoning @ Walmart claimed by salt ('...BerBere, Organic, with Salt...'); hamburger-buns @ Fareway claimed by onions ('Pepperidge Farm Onion with Poppy Seeds Hamburger Buns', plus Walmart's 'GV Sweet Hawaiian Onion Hamburger Buns'); canned-green-beans @ FF claimed by onions then garlic ('Del Monte Green Beans ... With Onion, Red Pepper & Garlic'); limes @ Walmart partially claimed by avocados ('Chick-Fil-A Avocado Lime Ranch...'); honeydew seeds claimed by oranges; mangoes claimed by peaches (a juice) and strawberries (a fruit-blend bowl). All released and re-landed correctly in the routing artifact, including the bonus catch 'Bush's Best Pinto Beans ... Seasoned With Onions' onions -> canned-pinto-beans.

AUDITOR NOISE (the rest): the audit's candidate matcher accepts garden SEED packets as cantaloupe/honeydew, 'Cascade Platinum Dishwashing Liquid Gel, Lemon' as lemons, 'Betty Crocker Lemon Frosting' as lemons, 'McCormick Kosher Celery Flakes' as celery, McCormick cilantro spice bottles as fresh cilantro, preserved-lemon jars, and fresh-cut trays as whole produce. These are not gaps; they are the audit's premise being looser than the engine's.

items.root_cause: audit-coverage-gaps validates candidates only against include/exclude regexes, while the engine also requires (a) a basis expressible in the commodity's unit and (b) the sanity band. The audit therefore reports as 'dropped stores' rows the engine deliberately cannot or will not price, and blames includes that are in fact fine. The real finds in the list are first-match claims by single-word commodities (the same class as item 0a87ef), which the audit ALSO cannot distinguish because it never simulates routing. This is the filter-divergence shape from the gates-that-can-never-arm family: the auditor measures a different pipeline than the one that runs.

root_fix.what: Make audit-coverage-gaps run every candidate through the same three gates the engine uses - first-match routing, Get-UnitPrice in the commodity's unit, Test-Band - and report each gap WITH its reason (CLAIMED-BY / BASIS-NULL / BAND-DROPPED / RULE-INVISIBLE). Only RULE-INVISIBLE and CLAIMED-BY page as actionable; BASIS-NULL and BAND-DROPPED are listed with their numbers without paging.

evidence: All 30 findings classified with the explain-coverage-gap logic (NO-INCLUDE / EXCLUDED / CLAIMED / MATCHES) against live rules. Four are real rule defects; the rest are variants invisible BY POLICY that need rulings so the sweep stops re-finding them.

REAL 1 - cranberry-sauce (FF word order): 'Ocean Spray Sauce, Cranberry, Whole Berry 14 Oz' and 'Ocean Spray Sauce, Cranberry, Jellied 14 Oz' ($3.79, as_of 08-01) are exactly the commodity ('Cranberry Sauce (canned)') written in FF's comma-inverted style, NO-INCLUDE because every include expects 'cranberry sauce' in that order. The rules-that-silently-disarm class: the store's name format defeats a word-order-dependent include.

REAL 2 - canned-pumpkin: 'Libby's 100% Pure Pumpkin Puree ... for Baking Pumpkin Pie Dessert, 15 oz / 29 oz Can' @ Walmart is the CANONICAL product of 'Canned Pumpkin (100% puree)' but Walmart's SEO suffix mentions 'Pie', and the exclude '\bpie\b' (which exists to keep pie FILLING out) eats it. Overbroad exclude, narrowed to '\bpie\s+(filling|mix)\b' so filling/mix stay excluded.

REAL 3 - frozen-lasagna: 'Stouffers Classic Lasagna ... Oven Ready, Frozen Dinners 19 oz' and 'Meat Lovers ... 34 oz' @ Walmart are frozen lasagnas eaten by exclude 'oven[\s-]?ready' (which exists for DRY oven-ready lasagna noodles). Narrowed to '^(?!.*\bfrozen\b).*oven[\s-]?ready': a name containing 'frozen' is a frozen dinner, not a dry noodle. FF's Rao's Meat Lasagna 27 oz MATCHES already, so its board absence is not a rule problem.

REAL 4 - laundry-detergent (FF truncation): 'Arm & Hammer Lndry Dtrgnt Fresh Scent Pls O' (130 oz, $13.99, as_of 08-01) is A&H Plus OxiClean liquid, the commodity's exact product, invisible because FF truncated the name. Narrow include '\blndry\s+dtrgnt\b.*\bpls\s+o\b' admits it; measured against all 22,341 names it admits exactly this one.

BY-POLICY (rulings, not rules): A&H Stain Fighters 32.5/100.5 floz (budget line, not OxiClean), A&H Clean Burst / Sensitive Skin / Baking Soda Fresh liquids (non-OxiClean lines), Plus OxiClean POWDER (form excluded on purpose) and 5-in-1 PAKS (laundry-pods commodity exists), Marketside/Simply Nature ORGANIC grass-fed 93/7 (exclude 'organic' is the price-comparability policy), Kroger 80/20 PATTIES (formed product), Smithfield SEASONED pork tenderloin x2 (one mojibake twin), Kroger SEASONED fries (plain-fries policy; Baker's cell already covered), Simple Truth CHOCOLATE almond milk (flavor variant), Ocean Spray Zero Sugar / Mixed Berry juice DRINKS (cranberry-juice cell already has all 7 stores), 'Kroger Unsweetened Tea' 1 gal $3.29 (real bottled tea, but the only admitting token would be bare 'unsweetened tea' which risks tea-bags collisions, and iced-tea @ Baker's is already the crown, so ruled instead of widened).

NEEDS BRAD - chicken-thighs: the commodity label is 'Chicken Thighs / Drumsticks' but exclude '\bdrumsticks?\b' bans drumsticks, which eats 3 real findings (Aldi 'Fresh Fresh Chicken Drumsticks Family Pack Per LB', Kirkwood, Tyson). The systemic answer to mechanism (1), normalized or order-insensitive matching, is a design change beyond this plan's scope; the rulings mechanism is the designed answer to (2) and is used here.
